response.markdown_report:
The recommended first experiment remains **position-dependent gating over NextItNet dilation depths**, trained jointly within one model per category. This is an incremental hypothesis; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users report that older, isolated purchases overshadow coherent recent behavior. Adaptive context weighting could reduce this mismatch, but does not guarantee historical exclusion. (2) Broad matches displace specific purpose or mood matches. Context selection may sharpen immediate intent; it cannot establish compatibility or distinguish complements from redundant purchases without sufficient evidence. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 lower-tail margin. Embedding similarity scores near 0.5 indicate mean pairwise cosine similarity near zero, providing no strong evidence of directional collapse; contextual discrimination is therefore a better-supported target than dispersion regularization.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) supplies causal multiscale features. [TV-Rec](https://openreview.net/pdf/e9c3bd1680a3ab54ffe119fc526e57d9835d7b8d.pdf) motivates adaptive convolutional processing without establishing gains here. (2) [Dynamic Layer Aggregation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.05770) closely precedes position-wise depth fusion; [SkipRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16518) supplies recommendation-specific adaptive depth. Novelty is consequently limited. (3) [Sampled-softmax research](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates moderate-temperature negative competition; [semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) motivates separate treatment of text and IDs. Neither establishes practical compatibility from available data.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Context selection targets stale intent; objective design targets confusing candidates; content integration targets item identity. These address different information gaps and should initially be tested separately.

Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell includes a positive and negative consideration. Alignment scores express hypotheses, not observed gains.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Learned dilation-depth gates | 3: focused convolutional adaptation / close precedents | 6: adaptable context / no guaranteed cutoff | 7: targets stale interests and broad matches / cannot verify fit | 6: contextual discrimination / weak margins may persist | 4: compact module / controls and serialization required |
| Moderate-temperature multi-negative loss | 3: focused objective change / established technique | 7: candidate competition / latent false negatives | 5: finer ranking / no explicit intent control | 9: targets weak separation / sampled gains may not generalize | 4: reusable scoring / exclusion bookkeeping |
| Joint scratch-trained title/ID gate | 5: constrained fusion / established ingredients | 6: identifiable cues / sparse text supervision | 7: specificity / similarity cannot establish compatibility | 6: extra discrimination / noisy features | 6: no external weights / tokenization overhead |

**Selected algorithm.** At 0% progress, retain depth gating as a small, testable intervention addressing two user failures: stale-interest persistence and broad matches displacing recent purpose-specific choices. It also targets Electronics’ weak separation. Multi-negative training is a strong subsequent alternative, but changing both would obscure attribution.

Retain causal residual blocks; consistently normalize their outputs and learn position-wise softmax depth weights initialized uniformly. Deep gate inputs can preserve dependence on old interactions even when shallow weights dominate. Test historical sensitivity through prefix perturbations; do not interpret weights as intent explanations.

Compare final-block readout, uniform fusion, learned fusion, and a parameter-matched final-block head as separate trials within budget. Hold other settings fixed; report all category HR@10 values, gate entropy/usage, parameters, training time, and peak GPU memory. Predeclare validation checkpoints and stopping rules, log every query, and freeze selection before hidden evaluation. If host-provided per-user hits are available, paired user bootstraps can describe conditional uncertainty; winner intervals remain exploratory and sampled-candidate HR does not establish full-catalog performance.

Preserve seeds, all four routes, fixed splits/evaluator, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. Mask padding within convolutional blocks, normalize channels, read the final nonpadding position, and serialize the identical architecture in the predictor writer.

idea.description: Add jointly learned, position-dependent softmax gates over intermediate dilation-depth features within the supplied NextItNet backbone. Treat this as an incremental adaptation of dynamic layer aggregation, with separate capacity and uniform-fusion controls.
idea.motivation: Test whether adaptive contextual weighting reduces stale-interest persistence and broad-purpose mismatches while improving the weak positive-negative separation measured in Electronics. These are proposed mechanisms rather than demonstrated effects. Compatibility, duplication avoidance, and HR@10 improvements remain unproven. Gate weights do not establish a short effective history because the gate itself can depend on deep contextual features.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected NextItNet baseline; its source is absent from this prompt, so this report specifies a reproducible architectural change rather than fabricating a drop-in training script. Keep its objective, sampler, optimizer, batch size, sequence length, precision, and backbone settings unchanged initially. Let K be the existing number of residual blocks and D their shared output dimension. Apply one shared, affine-free channel LayerNorm to each block output. Form the gate input by concatenating the K normalized outputs; use a single Linear(K*D, K) layer with zero-initialized weights and biases. This makes initial weights exactly 1/K. Sum normalized outputs using these weights, without another output normalization. Equal-width NextItNet states need no projections; if the supplied architecture has unequal widths, specify and serialize the required projections before comparison. All components are jointly trained within one network; load exactly one selected checkpoint per category. Separate control models are experimental trials and are never combined at inference. Controls are: the unmodified final-block baseline; uniform aggregation of the same normalized states; learned aggregation; and the same normalized final state with a residual MLP whose parameter count approximates the learned gate overhead, reporting any mismatch. Match controls on the unchanged backbone and training procedure. Count parameters directly and log realized receptive fields using R=1+sum((kernel_size-1)*dilation) over every temporal convolution, including both convolutions in two-convolution blocks. Use left-only causal convolution padding and channel-wise normalization. Zero padded activations before temporal convolutions and after each convolutional sublayer and block; masking only after a complete block can allow biased padded activations to contaminate valid positions in a subsequent convolution. Keep padded embeddings zero. Gate inputs must remain causal. Full-depth gate inputs intentionally permit long-history influence; shallow-heavy weights do not imply historical exclusion. Measure sensitivity by replacing valid items outside a prespecified recent window with other training-catalog items while preserving positions and the recent suffix, then measuring feature or score changes. A claimed guaranteed cutoff would require restricting both gate inputs and selected features to that window, which this proposal does not do. Track gate entropy, maximum-weight saturation, mean depth usage, and variation by history length on a fixed diagnostic sample; define saturation as maximum weight above 0.95. These measurements reveal behavior but do not prove faithful explanations. Report training time and peak allocated GPU memory at identical batch size, length, and precision. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts under the trial directory. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four datasets and routing, supplied splits, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch; respect the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget, including controls and diagnostics. Before running, fix the comparison order and retain the baseline validation schedule and checkpoint rule, documenting them explicitly from the supplied source; log every validation query and do not tune gates using diagnostic gains alone. Select exclusively by the pinned macro validation HR@10 and report every category outcome and the search trajectory. One additional validation hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If the host exposes per-user binary hits, use 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates with a separate analysis RNG seeded 2026: resample 200 users within each category with identical indices across compared models and compute each replicate's macro difference directly. Cluster by identity if users overlap across categories. These intervals condition on fitted models, fixed candidate sets, and the four datasets; they exclude training-seed and negative-candidate variation and do not correct adaptive selection. Label selected-winner intervals exploratory. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain unavailable outputs. Freeze the selected configuration before the host's separate final evaluation. Sampled margins are supporting diagnostics, not validation HR or full-catalog ranking evidence. Preserve ModelView.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items), with view.model referencing the actual trained module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Compute margins using the actual fused features and scoring head; define embedding-collapse measurements over the unchanged ID embedding table. Mark unavailable category breakdowns unavailable rather than inferring labels. Use only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions; reviews, ratings, prices, stores, categories, and simulator traits are unavailable. No timestamp or metadata input is required for this experiment. Preserve the native twenty-user diagnostic recommendation process and exclude seen items from those full-catalog recommendations. Update the embedded predictor writer with the exact model definition, gate configuration, normalization, and checkpoint keys. Verify checkpoint reload score agreement and causal behavior on synthetic sequences; handle empty histories using the corrected baseline's existing policy.
idea.pseudocode:
valid = sequence.ne(0)
x = item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
states = []
for block in causal_residual_blocks:
    # Block uses left-only padding and masks before/after temporal sublayers.
    x = block(x, valid) * valid[..., None]
    states.append(shared_channel_norm(x) * valid[..., None])
H = stack(states, dim=2)                     # B,L,K,D
logits = gate(concat(states, dim=-1))         # Linear(K*D,K), zero initialized
weights = softmax(logits, dim=-1)             # initially 1/K
features = (weights[..., None] * H).sum(dim=2)
features = features * valid[..., None]
loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
# Uniform control: weights = 1/K, without a trainable gate.
# Final-block and parameter-matched-head controls are separate trials.
# Inference uses the same log2feats and predict_score implementation:
positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
last = where(valid, positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
nonempty = last.ge(0)
scores[nonempty] = predict_score(features[nonempty, last[nonempty]], candidates[nonempty])
# Empty histories follow the corrected baseline policy; never index -1 accidentally.
# Select one checkpoint/category using the fixed host validation metric.
# Export architecture/configuration and verify loaded predictor score agreement.

originality.positive: Provides a focused NextItNet adaptation tied to observed contextual failures and tested with controls.
originality.negative: Position-wise layer aggregation closely precedes this mechanism, and SkipRec already studies adaptive depth for recommendation.

future_potential.positive: Offers a compact experiment for studying when different convolutional context scales help ranking.
future_potential.negative: Depth weights neither guarantee historical exclusion nor establish current intent; gains may reflect capacity or optimization effects.

code_difficulty.positive: The primary module is a small linear gate over existing equal-width block outputs.
code_difficulty.negative: Padding-safe sublayers, capacity controls, diagnostic adaptation, resource accounting, and predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Expanded receptive fields do not explicitly determine which historical context remains relevant to the next choice.

related_work.title: TV-Rec
limitations: Does not establish that dilation-depth aggregation improves this RecHarness benchmark.

related_work.title: Dynamic Layer Aggregation for Neural Machine Translation
contributions: Learns position-dependent combinations of intermediate representations, providing a close methodological precedent.
limitations: Studies Transformer translation models rather than the supplied convolutional recommendation task.

related_work.title: SkipRec
contributions: Studies recommendation-specific adaptive depth through learned residual-layer skipping in a NextItNet backbone.
limitations: Layer skipping differs from position-wise soft aggregation.
Does not provide the complete uniform-fusion, capacity, and memory control suite proposed here.

related_work.title: Microsoft Recommenders NextItNet implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for left-only dilated causal padding.
limitations: Does not substitute for inspecting and preserving the host's corrected baseline architecture.

related_work.title: Wu et al., sampled-softmax study
contributions: Analyzes how temperature changes emphasis on difficult negative examples.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal temperature or gains for the supplied NextItNet models.

related_work.title: Sequence-level Semantic Representation Fusion
contributions: Motivates accounting for differences between semantic and interaction representations.
limitations: Does not demonstrate that scratch-trained title features establish functional compatibility or improve this benchmark.

related_work.title: Selective Kernel Networks
contributions: Studies softmax selection among multiscale branches with branch-summation and capacity comparisons.
limitations: Vision results do not establish improvements for causal sequential recommendation or depth fusion.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired bootstrap resampling for statistics on aligned observations.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals do not account automatically for training randomness, adaptive model selection, or fixed-candidate sampling bias.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not quantify that disagreement for the supplied fixed RecHarness candidate sets.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation criteria and bias reported performance.
limitations: Ordinary uncertainty intervals around an adaptively selected winner do not remove this bias.
